title: ADL's Love for Family, Work and God
primary_topics: Eulogy for Alberto 'Bert' David Lina (ADL) delivered by CJP at his funeral Mass on Ash Wednesday, March 5, 2025
Three interlocking loves as the organizing thesis: love for family (especially wife Sylvia), love for work and country, love for God
ADL's 21-company empire and his 2,800 employees treated as 'partners and collaborators'
ADL's authentic Filipino rags-to-riches story: poor boy from Tondo with roots in Laguna, CPA-passer, rose to taipan through hard work and the school of hard knocks
sub_topics: Ash Wednesday context -- death as beginning of eternal life; Bert's smiling portrait as symbol of happy disposition
Extraordinary gifts to Sylvia: Jaguar car, Bösendorfer piano, special pink gumamela variety bred at UPLB, Sylvia P. Lina Theater at De La Salle Zobel Alabang
Love for four daughters (April Rose, Donna May, Lucia Jane/Sheila, Bertha Ann) and four grandchildren (Andy, Alwyn, Aurelia Joule, Aurora Jane)
ADL's business philosophy: 'back haul' system (fill returning empty trucks with cheap agricultural products), problems as opportunities not obstacles
Employee welfare: free daily meal with specially selected healthy brown rice, production bonuses and profit sharing regardless of rank
Government service as Customs Commissioner twice -- once under Arroyo, once under Aquino III -- against CJP's advice
Music patron: funder of Manila Symphony Orchestra, logistics sponsor of Philippine Philharmonic Orchestra and Metro Manila Concert Orchestra
Three operating principles: pakikisama, time discipline, being makulit (following through consistently)
ADL's Biblical-quote habit and 'love, not just like, your work' as twin threads binding his thought
Carillons donated to Manila Cathedral, St. James Church Alabang, Naga City, Pila Laguna, Mandaue Cebu -- symbols of mortality and God-dependence
Annual medical-surgical-dental missions, company bloodletting, support for Guiding Light Ministries of Aklan and Philippine National Red Cross
CJP's 1969 first meeting at L.C. Diaz audit of Baron Travel; wedding sponsor; 'daughter by choice' Donna May

stances.claim: The one word that unravels the secret of Bert's success is LOVE -- his enormous 'googolplex love' for his family, work and country, and for God. CJP uses this as his master key, not business acumen or capital.

Business persons have an obligation to treat employees as partners, not alalays -- Bert paid all 2,800 employees a free daily healthy meal and gave production bonuses and profit-sharing to everyone regardless of rank.
stances.rhetorical_move: labor-dignity principle embodied in named business practices

stances.claim: Problems are opportunities, not obstacles. The 'back haul' system is the canonical example of Bert's entrepreneurial reframing.
True wealth is measured not by what money can buy but by what money cannot buy -- integrity, honor, candor, truth, trustworthiness, and enduring love for God.
stances.rhetorical_move: dual-register wealth taxonomy: same credo CJP uses in RVR speeches

notable_anecdotes: Extraordinary gifts to Sylvia: brand-new Jaguar car; brand-new Bösendorfer piano; special pink gumamela variety commissioned from UPLB; Sylvia P. Lina Theater at De La Salle Zobel Alabang. 'Let us guess what he, if still alive, would have given Sylvia on her next birthday. A helicopter? A spaceship to fly her to the moon? The difficult, Bert could do immediately. But the impossible would take him a little while.'
CJP wore a pink tee shirt (Sylvia's favorite color) under his blue jacket at the eulogy -- the very shirt Bert and Sylvia gave him at a Bert-sponsored golf tournament years earlier.
Bert's 'back haul' system: fill returning empty cargo trucks with cheap agricultural products after delivering regular cargo -- transforming waste into opportunity.
Carillon donations across five churches: Manila Cathedral, St. James Alabang, Naga City, Pila Laguna, and Mandaue Cebu -- each chiming as a reminder of mortality and total dependence on God.
CJP and Bert first met in 1969 when Bert was a junior auditor at L.C. Diaz examining Baron Travel Corporation's books; Bert later asked CJP to be his and Sylvia's wedding sponsor.
'Daughter by choice' Donna May: she calls CJP 'Dad CJ'; CJP calls her one of his favorite dancing partners in waltz and swing.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered at Bert Lina's funeral Mass on Ash Wednesday, March 5, 2025, this eulogy by CJP opens by asking mourners to smile like Bert -- whose portrait reflects his characteristically happy disposition -- and frames death as the beginning of eternal life. The organizing thesis is a three-part love: first, love for family, especially for Sylvia whose extraordinary birthday gifts ranged from a Jaguar car and a Bösendorfer piano to a specially bred pink gumamela variety from UPLB and the Sylvia P. Lina Theater at De La Salle Zobel; his four daughters (April Rose, Donna May, Lucia Jane/Sheila, Bertha Ann) and four grandchildren. Second, love for work -- 21 companies, 2,800 employees treated as 'partners and collaborators, not alalays,' each receiving a free daily healthy meal and production bonuses and profit sharing regardless of rank, fueled by the 'back haul' system and a philosophy that problems are opportunities not obstacles. He served twice as Customs Commissioner (under Arroyo and Aquino III, against CJP's advice) and funded the Manila Symphony Orchestra. Third, love for God -- crediting the Lord with everything, donating Carillons to five churches (Manila Cathedral, St. James Alabang, Naga City, Pila Laguna, Mandaue Cebu) as reminders of mortality, and conducting annual medical-surgical-dental missions. CJP traces the relationship to 1969 when Bert was a junior auditor at L.C. Diaz, became his and Sylvia's wedding sponsor, and considers Donna May his 'daughter by choice.' The climactic one-word reveal -- LOVE, his 'enormous, googolplex love' -- ties all three themes together, closing with 'To God be the glory.'
